title: Go at the speed of wisdom
subtitle: Pace AI to the speed at which we can understand, verify and govern it: catastrophe would be permanent, while most of what delay costs can be recovered.
footer: Rufus Pollock · Wise AI briefing · Draft, October 2026
alt: Mindmap. How fast should we develop AI? Go at the speed of wisdom. Four reasons: the risks are real and contested; the world races because it is caught in a collective action trap; we should slow and steer, we partly can, and far more people should decide; wisdom traditions point towards restraint and are strongest on will and process. So every actor should push towards the speed of wisdom with its own lever.

root.label: How fast should we develop AI?

children.label: The risks are real
children.text: and contested, and the uncertainty itself calls for caution.
Four kinds of catastrophe threaten, and two would survive successful alignment.
The precursors became visible in 2026.
Experts disagree deeply on the odds, and we must decide anyway.

children.label: The world races
children.text: because it is caught in a collective action trap.
Each actor's reason to race is the others.
The race is accelerating, and restraint so far is mostly words.
Culture plausibly amplifies the race; structure alone would drive it.

children.label: We should slow and steer,
children.text: we partly can, and far more people should decide.
Slower at the frontier, faster on safety.
Restraint is possible, but AI is the hardest case, so start narrow.
The choice belongs to publics, not a few firms and two governments.

children.label: Wisdom traditions point towards restraint
children.text: and are strongest on will and process.
The direction is clear (don't be carried by the horse), though the pace is not.
Traditions build the will for restraint more than the mechanisms.
A wise process starts from intention and decides in concord.

children.label: So every actor should push
children.text: towards the speed of wisdom, each with its own lever.
Labs: accept binding external checks.
States: build verification, agree red lines.
Communities: make restraint legitimate.
Individuals: back pacing; insiders refuse to be carried.
